# rubberduck

The step between picking a ticket and ship start, for tickets that
aren't fully thought through. Research first, questions second, and
everything learned lands in the ticket itself — Jira stays the single
source, and the implementer may be someone else on another harness.
Never implements.

Needs a ticket key. Without one, stop: offer tickets (create one first)
or in-loop (explore without the workflow).

In ticketless mode (`Ticket source: none` in `AGENTS.project.md`, see AGENTS.md)
the input is a loose description instead: skip Read, run Research and
Grill as below, and Land writes only the plan file —
`plans/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` with the header `Ticket: none` — no
reconcile proposal, no tickets skill. Done when the file is written.

## Phases

1. **Read** — fetch the ticket (read call in
   `../ticket-platform/PLATFORM.md`): summary, description, status.

2. **Research** — in-loop mode (`../in-loop/SKILL.md`): delegate
   discovery to explorer subagents, keep the main context lean. Resolve
   everything the ticket and the codebase can answer: what already
   exists, which models/services/routes/components are touched, which
   acceptance criteria are already satisfied, obsolete or too broad.
   Never ask the user what code can answer. A question the codebase
   can't answer (library behavior, API facts) → offer research
   (`../research/SKILL.md`); its note feeds the grill.

3. **Grill** — grill-me rounds (`../grill-me/SKILL.md`) on what
   remains: genuine product and implementation decisions only — which
   existing concept owns the behavior, persistence, edge cases
   (deletion, reversal, refresh), v1 or a later ticket. An answer that
   raises a new code question → back to research before the next round.

4. **Land** — two halves, file first:

   **The plan file.** Write `plans/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<KEY>-<slug>.md` —
   exactly four parts:

       <header: ticket key, date, status>
       ## Steps        (numbered; each checkable — goal works and
                        commits per step)
       ## Decisions    (the grill's outcomes, each with its reason)
       ## Out of scope

   The file owns the "how"; the ticket keeps the what and why —
   nothing duplicated between them. A re-grill later writes a NEW
   dated file; the old one stays as history. The file lands
   uncommitted — it is committed as the branch's first commit (ship
   start / goal do this) and reaches main with the merge.

   **The ticket.** Draft a reconcile proposal for the tickets skill
   (`../tickets/SKILL.md`): the sharpened What & why / Acceptance
   criteria / Out of scope, plus one pointer line to the plan file.
   No plan content in Jira. Scope changes are part of the proposal: a
   split becomes new tickets with Blocks links; a ticket that turns
   out already done or not worth building becomes a close proposal.
   The tickets skill's gate is the only path to Jira — rubberduck
   never calls the API itself.

## Done

Done when the plan file is written, the proposal has passed the gate
and the tickets skill has reported the updated ticket(s) by browse URL.
Then offer ship start or goal.

## Boundary

- Never implement, never branch — that is ship's job. The plan file
  is the one file rubberduck writes.
- Never touch Jira directly — every write goes through the tickets gate.
- Ticket content in English, chat in the user's language — as always.
